key_insight: A learned steering agent can monitor LLM and multi-agent executions in real time, detect goal drift, and intervene to redirect systems back toward the task objective.
engineering_relevance: This adds a practical control layer for long-horizon agent workflows, improving reliability and efficiency without retraining the underlying executors.
method: Observes execution context and decides when to intervene using a low-cost fast path.
Uses a high-cost slow path to generate stronger corrective interventions when drift is detected.
Jointly trains drift assessment and intervention policies with reinforcement learning, combining pairwise ranking and GRPO.
evidence_signal: Experiments on information-seeking search tasks show improved performance and efficiency for both single-agent and multi-agent systems, with transfer to out-of-domain tasks and unseen executors.
watch_item: The steering policy must be integrated carefully to avoid unnecessary interventions or added overhead, especially when tuning intervention frequency.
paper_title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
